headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage via shared filesystem/MCP; Continue can write/read workspace files while Great Expectations consumes files and validation outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read/write workspace files and use MCP, while Great Expectations reads data sources and writes validation results/documentation. A malicious or malformed file produced by either agent can be treated as trusted content by the other through the shared filesystem path. This is a plausible default interaction, though not directly evidenced for this exact pair.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace directory, prompt-like content can cross from one to the other.
IF Great Expectations ingests documentation or validation artifacts generated by Continue, injected instructions can propagate.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Disable MCP servers not needed for the task.
Require manual review of any file-based instructions before execution.
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations inputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files exchanged between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches source code and open editor buffers and has broad network egress; Great Expectations touches data sources and validation results. If they share a filesystem, sensitive data can move from B's inputs into A's outputs or networked model calls. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default setups, but the exact data classes are not directly documented together.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains sensitive data sources or validation outputs, Continue can read them.
IF Continue sends copied file contents to a remote model provider, those contents may leave the host.
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of the shared workspace.
Use a local-only model provider for Continue.
Restrict Continue to a narrow project subdirectory.
Redact validation outputs before saving them to shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Great Expectations can install packages and read/write files. Both can mutate shared project state, so concurrent runs can overwrite artifacts or create inconsistent environments. There is no locking mechanism shown in either profile, so the conflict is plausible and not obviously prevented.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory, file overwrites or stale reads can occur.
IF Great Expectations installs packages while Continue is editing the environment, dependency drift can break runs.
mitigations: Run agents in separate clones or containers.
Freeze dependencies before concurrent use.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts.
Disable package installation during active editing sessions.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable paths.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can generate code or configuration that Great Expectations may consume as validation inputs, and Great Expectations can then emit validation results that a human or downstream automation may trust. Because neither profile shows built-in verification or provenance checks, errors can cascade from one agent's output into the other's actions. The interaction is inferred from documented file-based workflows.
conditions: IF Continue writes configuration or test code that Great Expectations later executes, mistakes can propagate.
IF downstream automation treats validation results as authoritative without review, incorrect outputs can trigger bad decisions.
mitigations: Add a human review step before executing generated files.
Compare validation outputs against a known baseline.
Keep generated artifacts separate from source-of-truth files.
Require explicit approval before any automated action based on validation results.
requires-engineering: implement provenance and checksum checks for exchanged artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and the profiles do not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Continue handles model provider API keys and editor/workspace content, while Great Expectations handles data sources and validation results, but no specific regulated-data pathway is documented. The other agent is not cited beyond the absence of a mismatch because no compliance conflict is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Continue's remote model provider, compliance obligations may change.
IF Great Expectations is configured to process regulated datasets under a stricter retention policy than Continue, policy mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of remote prompts.
Use local inference for Continue when handling sensitive data.
Document retention settings for both tools.
Review whether validation outputs contain regulated fields before sharing.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both tools.
